dedupe_keys.name: a climate database with varying drought heat signatures for climate impact modelling

description: The University of Bern and the Royal Netherlands Meteorological Institute provide six climate scenarios designed to isolate different drought and heat signatures in impact models. Each sequence contains 100 years of daily mean, minimum and maximum temperature, precipitation, shortwave and longwave radiation, and zonal and meridional wind. Coverage is a regular one-degree grid over land, excluding Antarctica and large parts of Greenland. Leap days are removed, giving 36,500 time steps per sequence. Zenodo distributes the NetCDF-4 variables and a readme freely under CC-BY-4.0. These are controlled climate sequences, not dated observations or probabilistic forecasts. That limitation matters when interpreting simulated failure frequencies. The data can test how simultaneous drought and heat affect water supply, cooling demand and energy resources. They complement observational climate products by varying the co-occurrence of extremes. No climate files were downloaded or simulations run.
